sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `__version__` is already `1.0.0`, but there is no `v1.0.0` git tag and the release has never been published. The CHANGELOG has a pre-written `[1.0.0]` section plus an `[Unreleased]` section holding ten shipped-but-unreleased changes (S114-S123). Before tagging, the changelog and version must reflect reality and the pre-release work (this slice's dependencies: CI on 3.14, the tamed verify warning, the schema contract, and the docs pass) must be done.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `CHANGELOG.md` (fold `[Unreleased]` into `[1.0.0]`, dated)
- `src/slicer/__init__.py` (`__version__`, confirm or bump)
- release notes / tag

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `CHANGELOG.md` has no remaining `[Unreleased]` entries that belong in 1.0.0; the `[1.0.0]` section is dated and lists the S114-S123 work.
2. `__version__` matches the tag to be pushed (the publish workflow keys on a `v*` tag equal to `__version__`).
3. The suite and `slicer check` pass on the release commit.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: This is the last step, gated on its dependencies. Fold `[Unreleased]` into `[1.0.0]` with a release date, confirm `__version__` (or bump if the accumulated changes warrant more than 1.0.0), and, once the owner authorizes it, tag `v1.0.0` to trigger the publish workflow. Tagging and publishing are the owner's call -- do not tag or push without explicit authorization.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Changelog and version are consistent; suite and check pass; the owner has confirmed the tag/publish.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: The tag/publish step is owner-authorized only. Do not tag or push otherwise.
